primary_category.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: Pulled her phone, found a breakup with her ex about three weeks back, some heated texts, and he had a prior domestic disturbance call at that same address
evidence.explanation: The detective retrieves and evaluates disparate evidentiary sources (phone records, scene condition, prior call history) to build a working case picture.

evidence.quote: We walk in already knowing the swab didn't match him.
evidence.explanation: Incorporating and weighing a new piece of forensic information against existing evidence is a core information-evaluation act.

evidence.quote: One witness closing a gap and one detailed description aren't the same as physical evidence tying someone to the scene.
evidence.explanation: The detective explicitly compares and weighs different evidence types for sufficiency, a hallmark of information evaluation.

evidence.quote: Get a working theory solid enough to direct the canvass without locking in before we had more to go on.
evidence.explanation: Formulating and adjusting an investigative theory to guide resource deployment reflects planning and non-routine problem resolution, not a fixed procedure.

evidence.quote: I named him primary anyway — the domestic history, the breakup timing, the locked door, that's a pattern worth acting on with the manpower we had.
evidence.explanation: The detective synthesizes multiple weak signals into an actionable resource-allocation plan under uncertainty, a planning/resolution act rather than routine execution.

evidence.quote: When I wrote the summary for the DA liaison, that statement got the most space and read as the strongest piece on the page
evidence.explanation: Composing a written referral memo that synthesizes case evidence for another party is a literacy-based communication task.

evidence.quote: It's usually a reminder to keep digging on the alternative rather than treating one result as the final word either way.
evidence.explanation: The detective generalizes from past cases to a broader principle about handling ambiguous negative evidence, indicating abstraction from experience.

evidence.quote: people moved on to warrant logistics for the ex fairly quickly... nobody was formally assigned to run down the loitering report
evidence.explanation: Deciding on task assignment, resource allocation, and priority-setting within the briefing reflects coordinating work among team members.

evidence.quote: We split canvass and paperwork like usual.
evidence.explanation: Dividing tasks between partners is a coordination activity.

all_observed_categories: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation
not_observed_or_insufficient: A1.1 Strength - no evidence of physical exertion described
A1.2 Dexterity - no fine motor/manual task described (evidence collection process not detailed)
A1.3 Navigation - canvassing mentioned but movement through environment not described
A2.1 Uncodified visual/auditory processing - scene observation mentioned briefly but not described as perceptual pattern recognition in depth
A3.1 Serving and attending - no direct service interaction with a member of the public shown
A3.2 Teaching, training, coaching - not present
A3.3 Selling and influencing - partner's persuasive framing exists but is the partner's act, not clearly the participant's own influencing task
ambiguities: A2.1 (uncodified visual information processing) is weakly suggested by the scene read ('No forced entry, deadbolt engaged from inside... that tells you something') but the text does not elaborate on the perceptual process enough to support it as a confident category; it is subsumed instead under information evaluation and conceptualisation.

A3.3 Selling/influencing is arguably present in the partner's forceful case-making at the briefing, but the participant (interview subject) is described as recipient/adopter of that influence rather than as the persuader, so it is not attributed to the primary subject's task content.

evidence.quote: I named him primary anyway
evidence.explanation: The detective exercises individual discretion in setting the investigative direction, though within a team and institutional structure.

evidence.quote: Reopening it right then would've meant pulling someone off the warrant work we were already moving on
evidence.explanation: Discretion is constrained by group consensus and resource tradeoffs, indicating moderate rather than high latitude.

evidence.quote: The DA liaison ended up asking for supplemental work before filing on either of them.
evidence.explanation: An external party (DA liaison) reviews and can reject the detective's referral output, indicating an external control/approval mechanism.

evidence.quote: once my partner and the lieutenant seemed comfortable holding the line
evidence.explanation: Supervisory presence (lieutenant) shapes the case direction, indicating a moderate monitoring/approval structure within the unit.

evidence.quote: my partner and I caught it together after patrol secured the scene... We split canvass and paperwork like usual.
evidence.explanation: The work is explicitly structured around a partnership and reliance on other units (patrol).

evidence.quote: My partner still laid out the domestic-call history pretty forcefully... One of the junior guys raised the rear-entrance lead again
evidence.explanation: Case direction is decided collectively in a briefing involving multiple personnel, showing high dependence on group interaction for key decisions.

evidence.quote: Just that nothing felt reckless in the moment. Every step had something behind it.
evidence.explanation: Each decision point involves distinct, non-repeating evidence and circumstances specific to this case, rather than recurring identical actions.

evidence.quote: We split canvass and paperwork like usual.
evidence.explanation: Some case-handling steps (canvass, paperwork split, briefings, referral drafting) follow a familiar institutional sequence, indicating moderate standardisation, though case-specific judgment dominates most decisions.

evidence.quote: nothing back yet at that point
evidence.explanation: Key decisions are made before forensic confirmation, under substantial evidentiary uncertainty.

evidence.quote: on their own, without independent corroboration, I didn't think they were decisive enough
evidence.explanation: The evidentiary picture remains ambiguous and unresolved throughout the case, indicating low certainty.

evidence.quote: Overnight, the lab actually gets back to us — negative, no DNA match to him at the scene.
evidence.explanation: New, unplanned developments (early negative DNA result, closed alibi, sharpened witness description) repeatedly require the detective to reassess the case theory.

tools.role_in_task: Forensic laboratory analysis (DNA swab processing) supporting the investigation

evidence.quote: We also swabbed the scene and pushed it to an expedited lab track
evidence.explanation: Use of forensic laboratory processing represents a specialised technical system beyond ordinary office ICT, even though the detective does not operate it directly.

tools.role_in_task: Case log maintenance and referral memo drafting

evidence.quote: the case log still had him as primary... When I wrote the summary for the DA liaison
evidence.explanation: Maintaining a case log and drafting a written referral document implies routine use of standard office/records systems, though the specific software is not described.

evidence.quote: Pulled her phone, found a breakup with her ex about three weeks back, some heated texts
evidence.explanation: Extracting communications from a mobile device is a digitally enabled evidentiary tool, though the specific extraction technology is not detailed.

task_anchors.task_description: Assessing physical scene conditions and digital evidence (phone records) to identify an initial evidentiary pattern.
Naming a primary suspect and allocating investigative resources under time pressure and incomplete information.
Group briefing reconciling a negative forensic result with the existing suspect theory and deciding on task assignment.
Reassessing the case theory against a closed alibi and a strengthened alternative lead, requiring a corroboration threshold judgment.
Drafting a written referral memorandum summarizing and weighting case evidence for the DA liaison.
